question.problem:
A discrete random variable $X$ has the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below.  Find $\text{E}[(X-1)^{2}].$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $0.6$ |
question.worked_solution:
For a discrete random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\sum }_{x\in S}r(x)f(x).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)=(x-1)^{2}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[(X-1)^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-1)^{2}\,f(x) \\  & =(1-1)^{2}\cdot 0.1+(2-1)^{2}\cdot 0.3+(3-1)^{2}\cdot 0.6 \\  & =0\cdot 0.1+1\cdot 0.3+4\cdot 0.6 \\  & =0+0.3+2.4 \\  & =2.7.\end{aligned}
$$
